name: content-registry-divergence
title: Content Registry Divergence
card: Give every page of a federated wiki (or any published set of documents) a name its content alone determines — the canonical hash of its title and story items, without the edit journal or item ids — fold the pages into per-site roots, a federation root and a chained registry root…
brief:
Give every page of a federated wiki (or any published set of documents) a name its content alone determines — the canonical hash of its title and story items, without the edit journal or item ids — fold the pages into per-site roots, a federation root and a chained registry root, and detect divergence between the living source and its published record by comparing like with like. Use when a wiki or document site should be checkable page by page, when snapshots should form a chain of their own, or when an edit in a fork should become dated, hashable evidence instead of noise.

A wiki's history is usually a log of revisions you are asked to trust. Name each page by its content and the log becomes checkable: anyone holding two hashes can tell whether a page moved, without either side showing the words.

- A published wiki, guide or document set should be verifiable page by page. - Each publication (snapshot) should commit to the one before it. - Someone edits their own copy and wants that edit to count as a signal against the published record.
